title: Dates, Time Zones, and Intl
summary: Represent a moment in time separately from how people read it.

subtopics.title: Store a point in time
subtopics.explanation: Store an instant as a timestamp or a clearly specified ISO string, then format it for the viewer when needed. A timestamp represents one point in time; it does not contain the viewer’s preferred display zone. For example, keep an appointment instant in UTC and format it in the user’s time zone.

subtopics.title: Understand time zones
subtopics.explanation: A time zone is a set of local clock rules, not always a fixed offset from UTC. Daylight-saving changes and government decisions can alter those rules. Ask for a time zone when scheduling a local event; adding a fixed number of hours can produce the wrong local time later.

subtopics.title: Format dates with Intl.DateTimeFormat
subtopics.explanation: `Intl.DateTimeFormat` formats a date using a locale and time zone. For example, the same instant can appear as `24 Sep` or `Sep 24` depending on locale. Pass an explicit `timeZone` when the display must be predictable, such as a meeting time shown to users in different regions.

subtopics.title: Avoid ambiguous date input
subtopics.explanation: Strings such as `03/04/2026` can mean different dates in different regions. Prefer a documented format, parse its parts deliberately, and validate impossible dates. Do not assume every date-only string represents midnight in the user’s local time; that assumption can shift a calendar date.

subtopics.title: Test time boundaries
subtopics.explanation: Test dates near midnight, month and year changes, and daylight-saving transitions. Those are the points where a time-zone conversion is most likely to show an off-by-one-day or duplicate-time bug. Include the intended zone in test cases instead of relying on the computer running the tests.

foundations.overview: A Date stores a timestamp: a point measured in milliseconds from a standard starting point. It does not store a user’s preferred time zone. The Intl API formats dates, numbers, and currencies for a locale.
foundations.mentalModel: A timestamp is a point on a global clock; formatting is the local clock face.
foundations.whyItMatters: Mixing time zones and display formats can shift appointments or confuse users.

keyTakeaways: Store instants consistently, commonly as timestamps or ISO strings.
A time zone describes local offset rules that can change.
Intl.DateTimeFormat formats dates for a locale and time zone.
